Policy documents often use the passive voice to describe societal failures, obscuring moral responsibility. Compare these semantic choices describing a neighborhood's economic collapse.

A central hub of economic power where the most important assets of the society are guarded securely. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->

El texto dice que el ritmo era dictado por "el sol y el músculo de los animales", lo que implica dependencia de la naturaleza y un ritmo biológico.

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v4`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Analyze

### Enunciado
In the second paragraph, the author describes city planning as "without planning." This suggests that:

### Options

options.text: Architects were very lazy and slept all day.
Economic growth happened too fast for organization.
The government wanted cities to look like forests.
Coal smoke made it impossible to see the maps.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El contexto de "rapid birth" y "thick soot" sugiere que la urgencia industrial superó la capacidad de los gobiernos para organizar las ciudades.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v5`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Analyze

### Enunciado
How did the Victorian middle class view the Industrial Revolution?

### Options

options.text: As a terrifying loss of their local traditions.
As a positive era of innovation and growth.
As a direct threat to their wealth and power.
As a boring time with no interesting changes.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El texto afirma literalmente que la clase media "celebraba el progreso y la innovación".

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v6`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
When the author states that workers became "extensions of a metal apparatus," he implies that:

### Options

options.text: Workers were given robotic parts for their bodies.
Humans lost their creative control to the machines.
Machines were designed to be friendly and helpful.
Metal was the only material used in the factories.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
La metáfora de "ser una extensión" sugiere que el trabajador dejó de ser el centro creativo (el maestro de su herramienta) para ser un engranaje más.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v7`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
What is the underlying irony presented in the final sentence?

### Options

options.text: That coal smog actually helped some people live longer.
That our current prosperity is built on a period of human suffering.
That village life was actually more expensive than city life.
That machines are now more intelligent than the people.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El autor contrasta el "motor de la riqueza moderna" con el hecho de que para quienes lo vivieron fue una transición "aterradora" de "alguien" a un "número".

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v8`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
The phrase "death warrant of the traditional agrarian village" most likely means:

### Options

options.text: Laws were passed to kill everyone living in the country.
The inevitable collapse of the traditional farming lifestyle.
Agrarian villagers were very happy to sign new contracts.
James Watt was a lawyer who wrote violent documents.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
"Death warrant" es una expresión idiomática que aquí indica que el invento del motor de vapor aseguraba el fin de la era agrícola tradicional.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v9`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
Which title would the author most likely agree with for this text?

### Options

options.text: "James Watt: The Inventor Who Saved Humanity"
"The Glorious Coal Age: Building Modern Britain"
"Dehumanization: The Unintended Legacy of the Steam Age"
"Urban Planning: Why Manchester is a Perfect City"

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
El énfasis del texto está en la pérdida de identidad ("someone" to "number") y autonomía, lo que apunta a la deshumanización.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v10`
**Type:** `multi-correct`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Analyze+

### Enunciado
Select ALL the socio-economic effects of the Industrial Revolution that can be inferred from the text. (Credits apply)

### Options

options.text: Massive migration from rural areas to factory-driven cities. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
A shift from craftsman-led production to machine-led labor. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
The immediate elimination of coal-based energy sources.
A disconnect between the workers and the final product. <!-- weight: 0.8 -->
A decrease in the total wealth of the Victorian middle class.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 6: El estudiante debe inferir de la "pérdida de autonomía" y el hecho de ser "extensiones" que hubo una desconexión técnica y social.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v11`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
When the author calls globalization an "ontological shift," what does he mean?

### Options

options.text: It is a change in the price of international products.
It changes our fundamental way of being and understanding reality.
It is a shift in the physical location of the national borders.
It is a temporary fashion trend that will disappear quickly.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 7: "Ontological" se refiere al ser/existencia. El autor sugiere que la globalización no es solo economía, sino un cambio en la percepción de quiénes somos.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v12`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
The term "cultural imperialism" in the text refers to:

### Options

options.text: Nations using armies to conquer other territories for culture.
Local people creating their own small businesses.
The dominance of global powers over local cultural identities.
A peaceful exchange where all cultures are equally represented.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 7: Inferencia léxica. "Imperialismo cultural" implica una relación de poder donde lo global (corporaciones) domina u homogeniza lo local.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v13`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
What is the "Global-Local Paradox" described in the final paragraph?

### Options

options.text: The difficulty of being globally connected while remaining locally unique.
The fact that global companies are actually located in local buildings.
The idea that local products are more expensive than global ones.
People wanting to travel globally but staying at home instead.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 8: Síntesis. La paradoja es el conflicto entre conectividad planetaria y preservación de la huella histórica individual.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v14`
**Type:** `weighted`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Create

### Enunciado
Which sentence best reflects the author's nuanced view on corporate globalization?

### Options

options.text: It is a double-edged sword that provides wealth but threatens cultural diversity. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
It is an inevitable machine of progress that should be embraced completely. <!-- weight: 0.2 -->
It is a purely destructive force that must be stopped by all nations. <!-- weight: 0.1 -->
It is a boring economic phenomenon with no impact on human culture. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 8: Reconocer "equilibrio retórico". El autor presenta ambos lados (supporters vs critics) para llegar a una paradoja, no a una condena o aplauso simple.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v15`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Evaluate

### Enunciado
What do the "local secret ingredients" of identity metaphorically represent?

### Options

options.text: Specific food recipes that global cities are missing.
The expensive products sold by local small companies.
The unique traditions and histories that make a culture distinct.
Chemicals used in manufacturing shoes in Portland.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 8: Traducción de metáfora. "Ingredientes secretos" simboliza la esencia única de lo local que está en riesgo de desaparecer por la homogeneización.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v16`
**Type:** `multi-correct`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Analyze+

### Enunciado
Comparing Context A (Industrial Revolution) and Context B (Globalization), what shared theme emerges?

### Options

options.text: The tension between technological progress and human identity. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
The loss of local autonomy due to large-scale systemic changes. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
The total superiority of urban planning over rural farming.
The transformation of individuals into parts of a larger network. <!-- weight: 0.8 -->
The idea that history always repeats itself exactly every century.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 9: Inferencia intertextual. El estudiante debe abstraer el tema común de la deshumanización técnica y la centralización sistémica que aparece en ambos textos.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v17`
**Type:** `single`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Meta-cognitive

### Enunciado
Which unstated assumption is necessary for the "cultural imperialism" argument to be valid?

### Options

options.text: That human diversity has intrinsic value that is worth protecting.
That all teenagers in Medellin dislike traditional Colombian music.
That corporate logos are more beautiful than national flags.
That people in Vietnam are richer than people in Portland.

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 9: Análisis de presupuestos lógicos. Para "criticar" la homogeneización, debes asumir primero que la "diversidad" es algo valioso. Sin ese valor previo, la crítica no tiene base.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v18`
**Type:** `weighted`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Create

### Enunciado
In "national culture becomes increasingly porous," the author implies that culture is:

### Options

options.text: Permeable and susceptible to external influences. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
Weak and destined to disappear entirely by next year. <!-- weight: 0.1 -->
Like a solid rock that cannot be broken by anything. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->
Becoming more focused on internal national security. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 9: El adjetivo "porous" (poroso) en este contexto sociológico significa que los límites de lo nacional permiten el paso de influencias externas (permeabilidad).

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v19`
**Type:** `weighted`
**ICFES:** Part 6 (Inferencial)
**Bloom:** Transfer+

### Enunciado
If the "Global Village" theory were applied to Martian colonization, a McLunhanist would predict:

### Options

options.text: That Mars and Earth would eventually share a single, unified consciousness through digital links. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
That Martians would declare war on Earth to protect their local rocks. <!-- weight: 0.2 -->
That moving to Mars would increase the distance between people. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->
That Martians would only speak Latin to be different. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 10: Transferencia. Aplicar una teoría histórica/sociológica (McLuhan) a un escenario futurista (Marte) para deducir una consecuencia lógica persistente.

---

questions.statement:
**ID:** `CO-ENG-09-history-001-PRO-v20`
**Type:** `weighted`
**ICFES:** Todas (Saber Pro)
**Bloom:** Transfer+

### Enunciado
The common thread through both texts suggests that the "Price of Progress" is often paid with:

### Options

options.text: The erosion of individual and local identity in favor of systemic efficiency. <!-- weight: 1.0 -->
The literal death of every person who lived in a village. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->
The economic success of everyone on the entire planet equally. <!-- weight: 0.4 -->
The complete destruction of all metal machines. <!-- weight: 0.0 -->

questions.explanation:
Pedagógica
Nivel 10: Síntesis final. El estudiante debe conectar el "número en un libro" del texto A con el "homogenizar la experiencia" del texto B para encontrar el tema central: la identidad vs el sistema.
